name: Kale and the Old City
tagline: Below the castle, among the copper bazaars
description: The historic core around the citadel mound, with the covered bazaars where coppersmiths still work, the Zincirli Bedesten, the old stone han courtyards and the restored Bey neighbourhood of cut-stone houses. This is the most atmospheric part of the city and where the baklava shops that made its name are concentrated.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the bazaars, the castle and the best food on foot
pros: Working copper and spice bazaars rather than displays
The famous baklava shops within a short walk
Restored stone houses and the citadel
cons: Earthquake damage and reconstruction are visible
Busy and congested through the day

name: Sahinbey Centre
tagline: The commercial heart around Ataturk Boulevard
description: The modern city centre north of the old town, with the shops, banks, offices and the tram line, plus the Zeugma Mosaic Museum a short distance west. It is where the practical business of Gaziantep happens and where most of the mid-range apartment stock sits, at prices below anything historic.
bestFor: Anyone who needs services and transport with the old city walkable
pros: All banks, shops and services close by
Tram and bus network through it
The widest rental supply in the city
cons: Air quality worst here in winter

name: Ibrahimli and the Northern Districts
tagline: Newer apartment complexes with space and parking
description: The residential expansion north of the centre, with modern apartment blocks, wide roads, supermarkets and schools. It is where Gaziantep's professional families have moved and where the newest and best-built housing is, at rents that remain low by any international measure despite being the top of the local market.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a modern, well-built flat and quiet streets
pros: Newest and best-insulated apartments in the city
Quieter and cleaner than the centre
cons: Twenty minutes from the old city
Car-dependent and short on street life

name: Sehitkamil and the University
tagline: Around Gaziantep University, students and cheaper rents
description: The northwestern district holding the university campus, with student housing, cheap eating and the youngest population in the city. Rents here are the lowest for a decent flat and it is the one part of Gaziantep where a foreigner has a reasonable chance of finding English speakers.
bestFor: Budget stays with the best chance of an English-speaking circle
pros: The lowest rents in the city
The most English spoken anywhere in Gaziantep
cons: Twenty-five minutes from the old city

name: Halfeti and the Euphrates (110 km east)
tagline: The half-drowned village on the reservoir
description: A village on the Euphrates about two hours east, partly submerged when the Birecik dam filled, leaving a minaret standing in the water and stone houses running down to a green reservoir. Boats run up the gorge to Rumkale. It is the region's most photographed spot and a genuine escape from the city's dryness.
bestFor: Weekends rather than a base, for the reservoir and the gorge
pros: The drowned village and the Rumkale boat trip
Green water and gorge scenery in a dry region
cons: Almost no services and no connectivity to speak of
Busy with Turkish visitors at weekends
